stem: How did Thoreau justify this act of civil disobedience?

options.label: A
options.text: He disagreed with increasing taxes for the lower classes.

options.label: B
options.text: He disapproved of increasing taxes to fund mainly urban areas.

options.label: C
options.text: He objected to tax money being used to pay for the U.S.-Mexican War.

options.label: D
options.text: He refused to provide tax money to a government that supported the Civil War.

visual_elements: I have paid no poll tax in six years. I was put into a jail once on this account, for one night. —Henry David Thoreau, Civil Disobedience, 1849
